clue.text: Smart surgeon's initial priority …

definitions.meaning: first meaning: neat and tidy in appearance
second meaning, read literally: the first thing a surgeon must make is a tidy incision

explanation.surface: A sharp surgeon knows what matters first, and the ellipsis runs on into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning is whimsical: a surgeon's first job is a neat incision. The ellipsis just links the surface to 5 across.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone neatly groomed and wholesome looking is described with this phrase, an everyday adjective for a tidy appearance.

clue.text: Risky location for company hiding a transgression

indicators.note: to hide something is to keep it inside, so the abbreviation for company wraps the rest

parts.note: Co is the standard abbreviation for company
taken as written
a sin is a moral wrongdoing

explanation.surface: A firm concealing wrongdoing is a dangerous place to be, a corporate scandal waiting to happen.
explanation.definitionFit: A gambling house is a place where people stake money and take chances, so a risky venue.

clue.text: Old military type deserting Essex after mutiny

parts.words: Old military type deserting Essex after mutiny
parts.note: surface reading: a rebellious soldier running away from his Essex barracks

parts.words: Old military type deserting Essex after mutiny
parts.note: setter's reading: a former soldier, someone who has left the service, with a nod to the last two letters of the county

explanation.surface: A soldier flees an Essex garrison after a revolt in the ranks.
explanation.walkthrough: No clean wordplay gives the letters. Read it as a description: someone who has deserted the forces is no longer in them, and Essex ends in the prefix meaning former.
explanation.definitionFit: A former soldier who has left the forces is described with the prefix for formerly attached to the service.

clue.text: After resolving our sins he provides support

indicators.note: resolving means sorting out or reworking, so the following letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A priest or saviour forgives our wrongdoing and then sustains us: a religious picture.
explanation.definitionFit: To feed and sustain someone or something is to give it the sustenance it needs, a kind of support.

clue.text: Off the record, international body had an impact

parts.note: the United Nations
something that registered made an impression or sank in

explanation.surface: An unofficial remark from a world organisation that still made a difference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off the record' suggests a confidential remark, but here it is literal: not entered in an official register.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not entered in an official register or list is literally not recorded, hence outside the official books.

clue.text: … it follows getting shot in bar

definitions.meaning: first meaning: something that pursues another thing
second meaning: the drink taken straight after a shot of spirits in a pub

explanation.surface: Continuing from 1 across, someone gets shot in a bar, as in a crime story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' suggests gunfire, but it is a small measure of spirits; the second drink that follows it has this name.
explanation.definitionFit: One who pursues is a pursuer by name, and a mild drink swallowed right after spirits carries the same word.

clue.text: Sweetheart changing name to Oscar? That's rubbish!

indicators.note: changing one thing to another means swapping a single letter for a different one

parts.note: honey is a term of endearment
N is the abbreviation for name
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at a partner wanting to rename themselves Oscar.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the N in HONEY for O.
explanation.definitionFit: Hooey is informal American slang for nonsense, meaning foolish talk or claptrap.

clue.text: Ridiculous, as diners get packed in like this

definitions.note: the answer completes the phrase packed in like ___

indicators.note: a ridiculous arrangement is an absurd muddle, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Restaurant customers crammed absurdly close together at their tables.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for being crowded tightly together compares people to small oily fish pressed into a tin.

clue.text: Shelters damaged tree covered in grasses

indicators.note: covered in means wrapped by, so the reworked letters sit inside the other piece

parts.note: to grass is British slang for informing; so does to rat

indicators.note: something damaged is knocked out of shape, so the word's letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written before rearranging

explanation.surface: A damaged tree overgrown with tall grasses gives cover, a picture of a wild garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grasses' looks like plants, but it is the verb: in British slang to grass on someone is to inform, as to rat is.
explanation.definitionFit: Retreats are quiet secluded places where one can withdraw for safety, so refuges or shelters.

clue.text: Excited at a rusty example of art

indicators.note: something excited is stirred up and agitated, so the following letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone gets thrilled by a rusty piece of artwork, perhaps an old metal sculpture.
explanation.definitionFit: Statues considered collectively form a branch of sculpture, one kind of visual art form.

clue.text: Detective finds headless writer in vessel

indicators.note: without a head means the opening letter of the word for writer is dropped
one piece sits inside the other, as cargo sits in a vessel

parts.note: a pot is a cooking vessel
a biro is a ballpoint pen, a writing tool; without its first letter

explanation.surface: A sleuth discovers a decapitated author stuffed in a container: a murder mystery scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer' suggests an author, but it is a pen: a Biro, the everyday British word for a ballpoint.
explanation.definitionFit: Hercule Poirot is Agatha Christie's famous Belgian sleuth, a fictional investigator of murders.

clue.text: Restrain characters promising rewards, if sent on

parts.note: to chain is to restrain
letters are written characters

explanation.surface: Holding back people who are promised a reward if they pass it along.
explanation.definitionFit: These are messages urging the recipient to copy them to others, promising good luck or money for doing so.

clue.text: Clouds naturally impair most bright images at first

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of each of the preceding words

parts.note: the initials of the five words

explanation.surface: Cloud cover naturally spoils most sunny photographs, a photographer's complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: Nimbus is a rain cloud or halo, and nimbi is its Latin plural form for several of them.

clue.text: Break down energy cable protecting fodder

indicators.note: to protect something is to surround and shield it, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: go means energy or vigour
hay is dried grass fed to animals
a wire is a cable

explanation.surface: An electrician's fault report: a power cable running through animal feed has failed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Energy cable' reads as one thing; split it, and only the cable wraps the fodder, while energy stays in front.
explanation.definitionFit: To malfunction or stop working properly, as a machine might, is the meaning of this informal idiom.

clue.text: Blast the city into pieces; it ensures fidelity

indicators.note: blasting into pieces shatters the words so their letters scatter and are reassembled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Bombing a city to rubble, oddly paired with a claim about faithfulness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blast' looks like the anagram signal, but it is part of the fodder; the signal is 'into pieces'.
explanation.definitionFit: A legendary medieval locking garment was supposedly worn to stop a wife straying while her husband was away.

clue.text: You get no thanks opposing such willing consent!

indicators.note: opposing asks for the opposite of each word in the polite refusal that comes before it

parts.note: the opposite of no
the word used when asking, the counterpart of the word used when declining

explanation.surface: A grumble that agreeing eagerly earns you no gratitude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No thanks' reads as ingratitude, but it is the polite refusal; turn it around and you have the eager acceptance.
explanation.definitionFit: The polite phrase for gladly accepting an offer expresses keen agreement, the reverse of declining.

clue.text: Quick way to eliminate cockroach perhaps

definitions.note: an exclamation urging haste, like the answer
definitions.meaning: first meaning: an order to hurry up
second meaning, literally: crushing an insect underfoot

explanation.walkthrough: 'Quick way' reads as one phrase, but Quick stands alone as a shout of hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom tells a driver to press the accelerator and hurry; literally it means to tread on a bug.

clue.text: Engineers rig sonar to show location of soldiers

indicators.note: to engineer something is to contrive or construct it, so the letters are built into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Army engineers set up sonar equipment to pinpoint troop positions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engineers' looks like a noun, the Royal Engineers, but it is a verb meaning contrives.
explanation.definitionFit: A garrison is a body of troops stationed in a fort or town, and the place where they are based.

clue.text: Relocate series for available players

parts.note: to transfer is to move elsewhere
a list is a series of items

explanation.surface: Instructions to move a run of items somewhere else, maybe a filing task.
explanation.walkthrough: In British football a club puts players it is willing to sell on this list.
explanation.definitionFit: The roster of footballers a club is willing to sell to other teams is known by this name.

clue.text: In France, here is the most remote

indicators.note: in France tells us the following words are to be put into French before joining them

parts.note: the French word for here
the French word for is

explanation.surface: Someone in France claims their spot is the farthest away of all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remote' suggests distance, but it means aloof or frosty in manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Icy describes a cold, aloof and distant manner, so the superlative is the coldest and most standoffish.

clue.text: Raleigh, for one, makes change after wife …

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for wife
to alter is to change

explanation.surface: A Tudor courtier transforms after marrying, and the ellipsis runs the story on into 22 down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts W in front of ALTER. Sir Walter Raleigh was an Elizabethan explorer and courtier.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Walter Raleigh the Elizabethan explorer is one example of a man bearing this first name.

clue.text: According to staff, medical department is secure

parts.note: per means according to, as in per instructions
to man is to staff, as a post or desk
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital

explanation.surface: Hospital employees reassure us that their department is safe and protected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' reads as a noun, but here it is the verb to man.
explanation.definitionFit: A job that is secure is lasting and not temporary, which is what this adjective means.

clue.text: … came to approve in great admiration

indicators.note: in places the word for approval inside the word for admiration

parts.note: awe is reverent wonder
to OK something is to approve it

explanation.surface: Following 20 down, a man regains consciousness only to approve, full of admiration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Came to' reads as arrived at, but it means regained consciousness.
explanation.definitionFit: To come to is to regain consciousness, as a sleeper does on waking, so this past tense fits.

clue.text: Badly crafted section stretches to cover inflated figures

definitions.note: a description of what the material does rather than a noun

indicators.note: a section is a part cut out of something, so the letters lie within the neighbouring words

parts.note: a run of letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A poorly made garment strains over a bulging body, a wardrobe malfunction.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is descriptive: this elastic fabric stretches over bodies, inflated figures being a jokey take on overweight wearers.
explanation.definitionFit: Lycra is the brand name for spandex, an elastic fibre used in tight sportswear that clings to the body.

clue.text: Failure to attend meal — that hurts

parts.note: nosh is British slang for food or a meal
ow is the cry of pain

explanation.surface: Skipping a meal is a painful snub to whoever cooked it.
explanation.definitionFit: Not turning up for a booking or appointment is known by this noun, also used for the absent person.

clue.text: Final trial reportedly overwhelmed witness

indicators.note: reportedly means as said out loud, so what counts is the sound of the next words

parts.note: beat means overwhelmed, and attest means to witness or vouch for

explanation.surface: A court case at its last hearing, where a witness is overcome on the stand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trial' and 'witness' suggest a courtroom, but the trial is a software trial and the witness is the verb attest.
explanation.definitionFit: In software development the last round of testing by outside users before release has this name.

clue.text: One can cure skin — or damage it, perhaps?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a worker who treats hides to make leather
second meaning: someone who tans, harming their skin by sunbathing

explanation.surface: A question about whether something heals the skin or harms it, like a sun cream advert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cure' looks medical, but it means preserving an animal hide; the second sense is a sunbather browning themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: A leather worker treats animal hides, and a sunbather browns and damages their own; both are called this.

clue.text: Person agreeing to put together dope record

indicators.note: putting things together means joining the two pieces end to end

parts.note: a dope is a fool, an ass
to enter is to record, as in a ledger

explanation.surface: Someone consents to compiling a record of drugs, perhaps for a police file.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dope' suggests drugs, but here it is a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: One who gives assent or consents to something is described by this noun built on the verb assent.
